scope: Private kernels and one preprocessing dispatcher over validated decoded BGRA bytes, explicit mode 0..3 and amount 0..3. Large-image working reduction is separately verified by image-resize-contract.json. File decoding, full cache lifecycle and GUI profile selection remain unfinished.
initialAlpha: Use the existing premultiplyClassifierPixels kernel exactly once before preprocessing. Preserve alpha.

enhance.dimensions: Positive integer width and height, exact BGRA byte length. Return an empty image with dimensions zero when either dimension is below 5.
enhance.border: Clamp each of the 25 row-major tap coordinates to the image bounds.
enhance.distance: In double arithmetic, compute red term (((Rc+Rn)*0.5+512)*dR)*dR*(1/255), then add 4*dG*dG, then ((767-(Bc+Bn)*0.5)*dB)*dB*(1/255), then ((767-(Oc+On)*0.5)*dO)*dO*(1/255). O=255-alpha. Accept only distance <2601.
enhance.accumulation: Accumulate each accepted BGRO channel times its integer weight into a float32 sum. Count is the sum of accepted weights. The center is always accepted.
enhance.normalization: halfCount=float32(count*0.5); reciprocal=1/count; byte=trunc((sum+halfCount-1)*reciprocal). Convert opacity back to alpha. Preserve this evaluation order.
enhance.ownership: Return owned output bytes and preserve the caller's input.
enhance.modeOne: Premultiply the initial decoded bytes once, then run EnhanceImage amount times for explicit integer amount 0..3. Amount zero performs no filter. An empty result remains empty.

reduceNoise.kernelWidth: 3 for amounts 0 and 1, 5 for amount 2, 7 for amount 3. Radius-zero sigma-0.5 kernel selection yields 3.
reduceNoise.border: Clamp each row-major neighborhood coordinate to image bounds.
reduceNoise.selection: For each independent channel, choose sorted sample index floor(kernelWidth squared/2). If the chosen value is the smallest unique value and another value exists, use the next unique value. If it is the greatest unique value and a previous value exists, use the previous unique value. A constant field remains constant.
reduceNoise.alpha: Native channels are BGRO. For odd neighborhoods, nonpeak median is invariant under the reversal O=255-alpha, so direct alpha processing produces the same byte.
reduceNoise.smallImage: If width or height is below kernelWidth, the native wrapper throws Magick::ErrorOption with reason ImageSmallerThanKernelRadius. The private kernel raises RangeError with that reason. Full application/UI exception translation is still unfinished.
reduceNoise.evidence: ../evidence/mode-two-boundary-investigation.json; REA 683, 685 and 687..688; captured first-chance native message in noise-error-message-native.bin.

despeckle.padding: Zero-padded (width+2)*(height+2) BGRO channel planes, initialized independently. Output ownership is separate from input.
despeckle.sequence: For each direction, run hull(forward,+1), hull(backward,+1), hull(backward,-1), hull(forward,-1).
despeckle.hullFirstPass: Read source center and source forward neighbor. Positive: increment if neighbor >= center+2. Negative: decrement if neighbor <= center-2. Otherwise copy center into scratch.
despeckle.hullSecondPass: Read scratch center and scratch backward/forward neighbors. Positive: increment if backward >= center+2 and forward > center. Negative: decrement if backward <= center-2 and forward < center. Otherwise copy scratch center to source.
despeckle.alpha: Convert alpha to opacity before filling each plane and back to alpha at output. Alpha padding must therefore correspond to opacity zero.
despeckle.amount: Mode 3 runs one DespeckleImage call for every amount 0..3; amount is ignored by the native dispatcher.

dispatcher.contract: Receive validated decoded BGRA dimensions, bytes and explicit mode/amount. Premultiply alpha once. Mode 0 returns owned premultiplied pixels; mode 1 repeats EnhanceImage amount times; mode 2 performs one nonpeak median with amount as radius; mode 3 performs one despeckle regardless of amount. Never substitute another filter or suppress an original empty-image/precondition outcome. No resize or file loading is inferred.
